fullText:
The 36-year-old woman charged with murder in a violent, high-speed crash that killed two people in Chatsworth on Tuesday was under the influence of drugs and had narcotics in the car when she drove the wrong way on city streets and broadsided a Metro bus, prosecutors said.

The Los Angeles County district attorney's office on Thursday charged Bailee Lynn Rios with reckless driving, driving under the influence and two counts of second-degree murder in the deaths of 46-year-old Daniel Castillo and 31-year-old Gage Weida, who was ejected from the bus during the crash.

"The tragedy of the Rios car crash was entirely preventable," Dist. Atty. Nathan Hochman said during a news conference on Thursday.

Rios was not charged in connection with the helicopter crash that claimed the lives of a pilot, an NBC4 reporter and a bystander. The helicopter had been hovering a few blocks from the traffic collision, providing a live feed for television news, when it appeared to suddenly lose power and crash.

Rios was scheduled to be arraigned Thursday in San Fernando court, but was not taken from the jail to the courthouse because of a medical event. She is now expected to appear in court on Friday, according to officials.

If convicted, she faces a maximum sentence of life in prison, Hochman said.

Video footage of the crash show Rios' 2004 Ford Expedition speeding on the wrong side of the road on De Soto Avenue, barreling through a red light at the intersection where the avenue meets Nordhoff Street, at roughly 5 p.m. The SUV narrowly avoids a car in the intersection before plowing directly into the side of the Metro Line 166 bus.

Rush hour traffic was moving slowly when Rios' Expedition entered one of the busiest junctions in the San Fernando Valley, but the SUV did not appear to brake before it T-boned the bus, witnesses said.

The impact was so powerful that the front end of the SUV nearly disappeared into the bus' frame. Castillo and Weida died at the scene. One passenger, who suffered severe injuries, and five others with non-life-threatening injures were taken to hospitals.

Rios mother, Cindy Rios, declined to comment to The Times when reached by phone on Thursday. But she told the Associated Press this week that she was sorry for the families involved.

"The fact that my daughter was involved and was the cause of it is just extremely disturbing," she told the outlet. "My daughter's alive. People lost their lives."

Investigators gathered video from a matrix of security cameras that surround the busy intersection to support their contention that Rios' actions amounted to murder with implied malice, according to law enforcement sources.

Authorities are also reviewing the SUV's event data recorder to determine Rios' speed, braking and acceleration in the seconds before the deadly crash.

That data proved key in prosecutors securing a double murder conviction in 2024 against Rebecca Grossman. In that case, prosecutors said Grossman was impaired by alcohol and Valium when she recklessly sped her Mercedes through a residential neighborhood, chasing her ex-Dodger boyfriend before killing two young boys in a crosswalk.

Prosecutors can prove murder charges based on someone's intent to kill or through a defendant's conscious disregard for human life, known as implied malice, legal experts told The Times.

"If you voluntarily behave in a manner that is so obviously and inherently dangerous to human life...a jury could say you're acting with a wanton and malignant heart," said Matt Murphy, a former Orange County homicide prosecutor.

Dmitry Gorin, a former prosecutor, said in this case authorities would be able to prove implied malice from Rios' driving.

"Here, the alleged wrong-way driving, high speed, running a red light, and near collision before striking the bus could be used to show she knew her conduct was dangerous to human life and continued anyway," he said.

The conduct and the resulting deaths would be a "very compelling theory for a jury to find her guilty of murder," Gorin said.

Court records and interviews paint a picture of Rios as a woman who had long been dogged by drug addiction.

Rios' friend Lanise Ward told The Times in an interview that Rios was sober when the two met for lunch about a month ago. She had been going to Narcotics Anonymous meetings and had been clean for the longest stretch since she began using drugs as a teen, Ward said.

"I really thought this time she was going to do it," Ward said. "She had been clean for a year and a half already."

In Simi Valley, where Rios spent much of her life, she had been arrested more than a dozen times by local police mostly on suspicion of drug-related offenses, authorities told The Times. However, the majority of the arrests do not appear to have resulted in criminal charges, Ventura County court records show.

Ward said Rios told her she began using drugs at 14 and struggled with an addiction to heroin. Rios had been to rehab several times, but couldn't seem to kick the habit long term until recently, Ward said.

Ward said if Rios relapsed she likely felt deep shame about it.

"I think she was disappointed in herself for getting high again, and I think she was trying to just end it all," Ward said.

In 2016, Rios was charged with possessing Xanax without a prescription and methamphetamine, both misdemeanors. The court dismissed the Xanax possession count and Rios pleaded guilty to the meth possession charge. She was placed on probation, ordered to submit to random drug tests and was referred to a drug treatment program, according to court records.

Less than a year later, she was accused of violating the terms of her probation, but was given a second chance and ordered to re-enroll in a drug treatment program. In 2018, court records show, she again violated probation and was mandated to a treatment program.

In 2019, she violated probation a third time and was granted conditional revocable release meaning if she got in trouble again she could face jail time, according to court records.

In 2022, Rios was back in court facing misdemeanor charges for being under the influence of a drugs, possession of heroin and Alprazolam, a benzodiazepine commonly prescribed to treat anxiety or panic disorders, and possession of an injection device.

She was also charged with an infraction for driving with a suspended or revoked license. The circumstances around her license suspension were not immediately available. Court records note that it was the result of an accident, but provided no additional detail.

A judge granted her diversion for four months, ordering that she enroll in a Narcotics Anonymous program, which she successfully completed, records show. She ultimately pleaded no contest to driving with a suspended license.

While Rios has no history of receiving a warning from a judge, called a Watson advisement—commonly issued after a driving under the influence conviction—L.A. County prosecutors have used warnings given by officers or others during traffic stops or other incidents to prove defendants showed a disregard for human life.

During the Grossman trial, a California Highway Patrol officer testified that he stopped her for speeding and warned that her that driving above the speed limit could have fatal consequences.

While prosecutors don't need a Watson advisement to prove second-degree murder it "is a very powerful piece of evidence if they have it," said defense attorney, Glen Jonas.

"Where there is no record of a court advisement, prosecutors scour prior reports and body cam footage to prove the defendant received a prior warning that her illegal conduct is in inherently dangerous to human life," Jonas said.

title: Trump-backed congresswoman criticizes his immigration policies
description: Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar (R-FL) talks to reporters following a House Republican conference in the basement of the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C.
fullText:
Rep. María Elvira Salazar, a Florida Republican up for re-election in November, released an ad on Thursday in which she criticized President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown, just months after he endorsed her campaign.

“Mr. President, some of your immigration enforcement efforts have gone too far,” Salazar said in the ad. “The same Hispanics who helped you get to the White House in 2024 feel betrayed today.”

"You can be for immigration what Lincoln was for slavery and Reagan was for communism," she continued. "I’m not talking about giving them amnesty. I’m talking about giving them a dignified life in this promised land. And only you can do that.”

The video marked a stunning break from the President who backed Salazar’s re-election bid earlier this year. In February, Trump said in a Truth Social post that the Congresswoman was “doing a truly fantastic job representing the wonderful people of Florida’s 27th Congressional District!” and that she “knows the Wisdom and Courage required to confront the Corrupt Fake News.” He said that she had his “Complete and Total Endorsement for Re-Election” before telling voters that Salazar “WILL NEVER LET YOU DOWN!”

Salazar joins a growing number of Republicans who have publicly pushed back on Trump’s policies.

Trump has railed against other members of his party who have broken with him, going so far as to endorse several of their challengers in the primaries. The President endorsed Ed Gallrein, for instance, who ultimately defeated Rep. Thomas Massie in the May Republican primary for the Kentucky Congressman’s seat, after Massie broke with Trump on various issues, including objecting to the “One Big Beautiful Bill” and leading the effort to push the Department of Justice to release the so-called “Epstein files.”

Salazar’s campaign said that the video released on Thursday is the first of multiple ads that it plans to run before the upcoming midterm elections, in which Salazar is facing off against Democratic nominee Eliott Rodríguez. Both Salazar and Rodríguez are Cuban American, and previously worked as journalists.

Rodríguez criticized Salazar for the ad in a video that he shared on social media on Thursday, claiming that she had "desperately sought Donald Trump's endorsement" but was now speaking out "because [Trump's] immigration policy is political poison in her re-election campaign." Rodríguez went on to accuse his Republican opponent of being a "pathetic rubber stamp for Donald Trump."
"María Elvira Salazar did this—make no mistake about it," Rodríguez said. "She owns all of these deportations, ICE harassment, family separations, and racial profiling. She voted for it. She gave Donald Trump the money and the tools to do it. Now, just 47 days before the midterm election, she is trying to convince voters that she disagrees with Trump's inhumane practices on undocumented people with no criminal record."

The Cook Political Report indicates that Salazar, a three-term Congresswoman, is expected to hold on to her seat come November, rating it as “Likely Republican.”

In the district Salazar represents, the foreign-born population makes up more than 54% of the total population—one of the largest proportions of all the districts in the lower chamber.

Thursday’s ad isn’t the first time that Salazar has expressed concerns about the Trump Administration’s immigration enforcement efforts. Earlier this week, she responded to reports that Luis Galeano, an exiled Nicaraguan journalist whose U.S. asylum application has been pending for years, had been detained by federal immigration agents.

“America must always know the difference between a criminal and a political exile,” Salazar said in a statement shared on social media. “Luis is a respected journalist who paid a price for telling the truth about the Ortega-Murillo dictatorship. The regime persecuted him, forced him into exile, and stripped him of his citizenship. That history matters. He cannot be sent back into the hands of the people who targeted him.”

“I have been clear with the Administration: enforce the law and deport dangerous individuals, but do not treat political exiles like criminals,” she continued.

Salazar has also been backing a bipartisan measure in the House that would grant immigrants who don’t have a criminal history a route to secure legal status in the U.S., but not a pathway to citizenship.

title: 10 Hacks Every Vivaldi Browser User Should Know
description: Use these hacks to make the most of Vivaldi.
fullText:
When you think about browsers, Vivaldi is probably not the first name that comes to mind—but it should be. This is a Chromium-based browser that focuses on adding so many features that you don't need to install multiple apps to get things done. Vivaldi has been around for over a decade now, and has become a pretty complete product, though it continues to improve. I've been using the browser for while, and these are the best Vivaldi hacks I've found in my time.

Vivaldi for Android, one of the best non-Chrome browsers on Android, recently added support for Chrome extensions—even though Chrome for Android still doesn't support extensions. You can use it to enhance your privacy by installing uBlock Origin Lite to block ads and tracking. You should also consider using Decentraleyes to evade tracking through centralized content delivery networks, and SponsorBlock to skip sponsored segments in YouTube videos. That said, all your favorite extensions should work here, and they're pretty easy to install on Vivaldi for Android. Just tap the puzzle piece icon in the address bar, and you'll see a menu that allows you to open the Chrome Web Store.

"Workspaces" allow you to separate tabs by project, like folders for your browser tabs. For instance, if you have a few sites open for work, you can group them under a separate workspace. I've created a workspace called "Research" to group all the tabs I use to compile my articles, and similarly, I have workspaces to group my long reads, distractions, and social media. To get started, click the Workspaces button in the tab bar, and select New Workspace. Give it a name, and start adding tabs to the workspace. You can right-click any open tab, and select Move > Workspace.

"Follower Tabs" allow you to go down rabbit holes without losing track of the original page. I often get lost when clicking different links on articles and websites. Vivaldi's Follower Tabs allow me to keep the original page open in a split-screen view while I read the context links, and I can quickly return to reading the original page. To use this feature, open any webpage, right-click a link, and select Open Link in > Open Link as Tiled Follower Tab. You can also open any link in split-screen view by right-clicking the link, and selecting Open Link in > Open Link as Tiled Tab.

Vivaldi's "Quick Commands" feature is a lot like Mac's Spotlight Search. Both allow you to make calculations, find settings, and execute automation commands. In Vivaldi, you can open the Quick Commands popover by pressing F2 or Ctrl-E (Command-E on Mac). You'll see a long list of commands here: The search box at the top allows you to look for specific commands, but you can get started by performing basic math, toggling the status bar, or even running a niche command like "Copy all links," which copies the URLs of all of your open tabs.

Vivaldi also supports some degree of automation through Command Chains. You can find this feature by clicking the Vivaldi button in the top-left corner of the browser (the exact position may vary depending on your layout), and selecting Settings > Quick Commands. Under "Command Chains," you'll be able to see a few examples of these automations, and you can click the + button to create your own. I like the simple "Toggle Fullscreen and Reader View" Command Chain for quick distraction-free reading. Once set up, you can run Command Chains by using the Quick Commands feature described above. Press F2, and search for the name of the Command Chain.

Vivaldi also allows you to customize most menus in the browser, including the right-click menu. I never use the Back/Forward buttons in these menus, and I find a few other options redundant, so I like adding features I'll actually use, such as "Find in Page." To do this, go to Vivaldi Settings > Appearance, and scroll down to the "Menu Customization" section. Use the drop-down menu to select Page, where you can add commands from the right pane. Right-click any command in the left pane, and select "Delete" to remove it. You can also reorder options, add a separator, subfolders, and so on. If you accidentally change things too much, you can always use the Restore Default Menu button on this page for a reset.

Vivaldi has a mode called "caret browsing," which shows a blinking cursor on any webpage, and allows you to use the arrow keys to browse the page, copy text, links, and images. This lets you use the browser without touching the mouse, similar to how keyboard navigation works in apps like Google Docs or Microsoft Word. You can toggle this feature on any page in Vivaldi by pressing Shift-F7.

Similarly, you can also create mouse gestures in Vivaldi to replace keyboard navigation. Go to Vivaldi Settings > Mouse, and check out the gestures under "Gesture Mapping." You can hit the + button to create your own gesture and link it to a browser command of your choice. To perform a gesture, just hold the right-mouse button, then move the cursor in the pattern you've recorded.

Vivaldi allows you to prolong battery life by using its Energy Saver and Memory Saver features. Go to Vivaldi Settings > Performance to view your options. Under "Energy Saver," you can enable Turn On at 20% Battery or Lower. I also recommend using Balanced Savings in "Memory Saver," which frees up RAM by unloading inactive tabs. This prevents the browser from slowing down, and as a result, enhances your battery life.

If you're constantly refreshing news websites or your social media feeds, you can automate that action with Vivaldi. Just right-click any open tab, select Periodic Reload, and choose a time interval. The browser allows you to refresh the page once every minute, two minutes, all the way up to once every 90 minutes.

title: Leaden, stale, disheartening - where do Celtic & O'Neill go from here?
description: After another defeat, keeping the faith is surely becoming more testing for Celtic's fans, writes Tom English.
fullText:
To Celtic fans it might seem like sacrilege to doubt Martin O'Neill's capacity to get them through whatever it is they're going through right now - a slump or something deeper - but keeping the faith is surely becoming testing.

After their shellacking at Ibrox on Sunday, Celtic's response against Ferencvaros was another heavy defeat and three more goals conceded.

More absent-minded stuff in the midfield, more loose defending, more negativity and lack of accuracy on the ball, no great grasp of the basics of pass and move, not enough intensity, not enough work-rate, not enough of anything that you need to give yourself a chance.

At times, as it meandered along at 3-1 to Ferencvaros, Celtic tried to stage some kind of gallop but their attempts were from distance, hopeful efforts rather than anything built on the back of coherence and pressing and speed.

Celtic at their best - in the finest days under Ange Postecoglou - were all about aggression and ingenuity, about dynamism and risk-taking, about pace and belief and pulling defenders into places where they did not want to be.

Fragile Celtic beaten by Ferencvaros in Europa League opener

Celtic are 'little bit broken' - but is change of shape 'worth risking'?

Reaction, analysis & have your say on Celtic's defeat

Things can turn quickly in Scottish football.

The second act of this season's Old Firm show on Sunday is still a hard one to call, partly because it's at Celtic Park and also because there surely has to be some kind of response from O'Neill's team to their pitiful fate at Ibrox last weekend.

Their fans will be worried, though. Five goals given up against LASK, a desperate experience at Ibrox - and now this.

In moments on Thursday, some of their football was reminiscent of darker days - the failures of Cluj and Copenhagen in 2019 and 2020, when Bayo and Bolingoli were in the building; Sparta Prague in 2020, when Klimala and Ajeti, Duffy and Laxalt were in the team.

It was all very Legia Warsaw, very Salzburg, very Maribor. The energy levels were low, the booing was loud and the feeling of a side with no answers was unmissable.

In the aftermath, O'Neill spoke about frustration, failure and psychological damage, how low moments like these hit you hard and test your resolve. He promised to "get ourselves together" for Rangers on Sunday but his tone was flat and a touch tired.

He outlined some of the ways in which Celtic were deficient on the night but didn't talk with the spirit of a man who had answers. In many ways his post-match comments mirrored his team's performance - leaden, stale, disheartening.

O'Neill has fixed many problems over the years, not just in his first trophy-laden spell but in his return to chaos last season. He restored order and confidence, two things that have been lost.

The force of his personality gave Celtic fight. They were not always pretty to watch but they were ferociously hard to beat. Nobody managed it on the title run-in.

That kind of never-say-die only seems like yesterday, but in other ways it feels like an awfully long time ago.

They had a decent start against Ferencvaros, then conceded a soft goal. They hauled themselves back into it with a little glimpse of quality, but then fell back into destructive ways. Safe passes, little zeal, only a modicum of fire and emotion.

The goal they conceded just before the break was the type of goal that poor sides give away. Hesitancy in the first instance to fight for the loose ball, weakness in the second instance when trying to prevent the cross and then defensive disorganisation and bewilderment in the end.

Celtic had 62.5% possession in the opening half but trailed 2-1. Camilo Duran, playing through the middle ahead of Kasper Hogh, had eight touches of the ball.

Duran was in his favoured position but offered little. A player who showed such zest and love of his new life in Glasgow only a few short weeks ago is looking a shadow of himself.

Hogh, with goals against Man City (two), Atletico Madrid, Inter Milan, Sporting, Porto, Jagiellonia and Olympiacos (three) for Bodo Glimt, has morphed into an awkward looking centre-forward with a poor first touch and no chances to feed on.

He has now scored in just one of his eight games as a Celtic player. O'Neill has so far failed to get the best out of a player the club paid £11m for.

Callum McGregor, the great totem, is looking a little lost. O'Neill has all the nous in the world to arrest this, but he needs to do it quickly. It has to be said, he doesn't look or sound all that convincing.

The way things are going for Celtic you could almost have guaranteed a goal for Daniel Arzani, their former player who came and went in a blur of nothingness.

To add salt, it was a magnificent strike after a counter-attack that exposed Celtic in the most embarrassing way. There was more order in the Keystone Cops.

Arzani appeared in acres of space on the left, Colby Donovan having over-committed to attack and now busting a gut in a forlorn attempt to recover. Arzani had patience and precision. He whipped his shot into the top corner. Easy.

O'Neill needs some amount of solutions in the coming days. Football is weird. He might find them, but his team is lacking ideas, conviction, composure, physical and psychological heft, creativity, ruthlessness and stomach for a fight.

The manager, himself, looks like he's lacking in any inspiration. He's bounced back from challenging situations in his football past and you almost become attuned to him doing so again, but there is a lot to fix here.

McGregor says the team is a little bit broken at the moment. Rangers might be licking their lips at the prospect of facing a wounded animal. Beware the backlash and all of that, but they have an opportunity to land another blow.

Sunday will tell us much about the way of things between the Glasgow giants.

title: Six-time Grand Slam champion Salisbury retires
description: Former world number one doubles player and six-time Grand Slam doubles champion Joe Salisbury retires from professional tennis.
fullText:
Former world number one doubles player and six-time Grand Slam doubles champion Joe Salisbury has retired from professional tennis.

Londoner Salisbury chose this month's US Open as his final event and reached the semi-finals with his long-time partner Rajeev Ram, who had also decided to retire.

The venue was fitting, as in 2023 Salisbury and Ram became the first pair in history to win three consecutive US Open men's doubles titles.

Salisbury is Britain's most successful men's doubles player of the Open era. He also won the 2020 Australian Open with Ram, and two mixed doubles titles with Desirae Krawczyk.

The 34-year-old says he has been thinking about his future for a while, and is now "very happy with the decision".

"Tennis has been my life for as long as I can remember and I have been incredibly fortunate to have had all the opportunities, experiences and success that I have," he posted on Instagram.

"To be able to travel the world and call playing tennis my job has been a dream come true and I never believed I could have lived the life and had the career that I have.

"I gave it my all and know I can be proud and look back with no regrets."

Salisbury took a three-month break at the start of this year, having told BBC Sport about the anxiety which had been affecting him on tour.

While he did not think it affected his tennis very much, he said it left him with a "feeling of dread" which made life on the road far less enjoyable.

"I had some time off for a few months earlier on in the year - I wasn't really enjoying being on tour for a few reasons," he told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"I came back and I didn't really have a successful year. Then I teamed back up with my partner, Rajeev Ram, who I had all my success in Grand Slam titles [with] so it was great playing with him again and he was retiring at the US Open this year.

"I thought I could go on [until the] end of this year, maybe next year but I felt like it was nice to finish my career playing with him at the US Open where we had our success, and we had a good run making the semi-finals to finish."

Salisbury finishes his career with 17 tour level titles, including the season-ending ATP Finals of 2022 and 2023.

title: McIlroy falters as Rai shares lead at Wentworth
description: Aaron Rai shoots a six-under 66 to share the first-round lead with Sweden's Joakim Lagergren at the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth as Rory McIlroy suffers a late stumble.
fullText:
BMW PGA Championship - round one

-6 A Rai (Eng), J Lagergren (Swe); -5 R Gerard (US), A Scott (Aus), I Elvira (Spa), L Aberg (Swe)

Selected others: -4 P Reed (US), R Fox (NZ), R MacIntrye (Sco), V Hovland (Nor), T Detry (Bel); -3 R Fisher (Eng), R McIlroy (NI), D Law (Sco), A Sullivan (Eng), E Ferguson (Sco), J Dean (Eng); -2 T Hatton (Eng), JJ Spaun (US); -1 S Lowry (Ire) -1 M Wallace (Eng); E A Fitzpatrick (Eng), M Fitzpatrick (Eng)

While Rory McIlroy sparkled and then suffered a late stumble, Aaron Rai was a model of consistency as he shot a six-under 66 to share the first-round lead with Sweden's Joakim Lagergren at the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth.

Rai, who became England's most recent major winner earlier this season, knocked in seven birdies, with the only blemish to his card arriving on the 16th, when he found the fairway bunker off the tee and ended with a bogey five.

Lagergren, whose one and only win on the DP World Tour was back in 2018, also made a fine start with an eagle on the 12th, the highlight of his round.

Six-time major winner McIlroy had got under way in sensational fashion earlier in the day until his round unravelled on the back nine.

The Northern Irishman was five under after 10 holes and in the outright lead but some erratic driving proved costly after the turn on a course he covered in 60 in Wednesday's pro-am.

And when McIlroy also found the water on his penultimate hole, it contributed to one of his three bogeys in the final seven - leaving him at three under, three strokes adrift of the joint-leaders.

American Ryan Gerard, Australia's Adam Scott, Spain's Nacho Elvira and Sweden's Ludvig Aberg are at five under, while Patrick Reed, the only player above McIlroy in the Race to Dubai standings, is one of 12 players at four under.

Reed, who is bidding to become only the second American after Collin Morikawa to win the Race to Dubai, is in a group two shots off the lead with Open champion Ryan Fox, Norway's Viktor Hovland and Scotland's Robert MacIntyre, who made birdies on the 17th and 18th holes to conclude with a flourish.

However, it was a difficult day for Spain's two-time major winner Jon Rahm, who carded a six-over 78.

Birdies proved difficult to come by as Rahm played alongside Justin Rose and Tommy Fleetwood, with none of the trio picking up a single shot on the front nine.

While the English duo were able to make five birdies between them on the back nine to finish at one over, Rahm toiled to five bogeys and a double bogey as he repeatedly found trouble off the tee.

Former US Open champion Matt Fitzpatrick, who outlined his reluctance to travel to Dubai for November's season-ending DP World Tour Championship event on Wednesday, is at level par, along with his younger brother Alex.

title: Fin Smith sets England autumn ultimatum to hit form
description: England fly-half Fin Smith says an under-par autumn would trigger fundamental questions about the team's direction.
fullText:
England fly-half Fin Smith says an under-par autumn should trigger fundamental questions about the team's direction.

The 24-year-old was asked by Rugby Union Weekly about the state of the team after a miserable Six Nations and a summer campaign that featured a 45-21 defeat by world champions South Africa, a 73-8 thrashing of Fiji and a narrow 31-24 win over Argentina.

"It is so hard to say," replied Smith.

"I am not going to sit here and say 'we are building' because that is what you will get every time.

"We will honestly find out in the autumn. If we have a pretty ropey autumn, on the back of building some momentum over the summer, I think we will need to have a pretty hard look at ourselves."

England will play Australia, Japan and New Zealand on successive weekends in November, before a play-off against a southern hemisphere opponent in the finale of the new Nations Championship competition.

"Playing New Zealand at Allianz Stadium will be a great way to test ourselves," said Smith.

"I think on our day, in front of a big crowd and when we are up for it, we can beat anyone. The last time New Zealand came we had a great result."

England beat the All Blacks 33-19 last November in arguably the high point of head coach Steve Borthwick's near four-year spell in charge.

However the team's form has tailed off in 2026, with only three wins in eight Tests. A chastening 42-21 defeat at home by Ireland and a first-ever loss to Italy were among the low points.

Smith, who has started the past five Tests to establish himself as first-choice stand-off ahead of George Ford and Marcus Smith, says he is getting aligned with the demands of Test rugby and Borthwick's gameplan.

"I have been given a fair bit of licence to put my footprint on the attack and lead a lot of meetings about how I want us to play," he said.

"England are probably set up in a slightly different way. Northampton would probably be slightly more attacking and set up with maybe a slightly lighter-weight forward pack that might be suited to the style of play there.

"England is a little bit more set-piece and arm wrestle and tactical, so I have to adapt my game to suit that as well.

"But most of the time I am just going out there to just play what I see."

Marchant set on England comeback after Sale arrival

Rugby Union Weekly: Fin Smith, LRZ, JVP & more!

Smith's Northampton boss Phil Dowson has said he has aspirations to eventually coach internationally, having racked up four impressive seasons in charge at Franklin's Gardens.

As director of rugby, the 44-year-old has led Saints to two Prem titles and the 2025 Champions Cup final.

That success has shown in England's selections. Northampton provided six players – more than any other club - to England's Nations Championship squad this summer.

"Fundamentally, we are having a great time at Northampton," Dowson said of himself and head coach Sam Vesty.

"From a personal point of view, at some point, we'd like to coach international rugby because it is different.

"There's no timeline on that. That's not just England. It is just the opportunity to go and do something different to test ourselves - either as a team or individually - under different pressure and to have new experiences."

Dowson said there has been no contact from the Rugby Football Union about preparing him for such an opportunity with England.

He prepared a developmental England XV's forwards, external for a fixture against the Barbarians in May 2019, but has not been brought into the fold since.

Vesty, meanwhile, was seconded to be the attack coach for England A's 91-5 rout of Portugal in February 2024. Back in 2017, he also stepped in as skills coach under Eddie Jones for England's summer tour to Argentina.

Both men signed new contract extensions with Northampton in December.

title: From -17 points to dream European start for Bournemouth
description: Bournemouth started a League Two season on -17 points in 2008, now they have made a dream start in European competition.
fullText:
'From -17 to Europe', read a flag in the away end at at the Anoeta Stadium.

As Bournemouth embarked on the first European campaign in the club's 127-year history, it served as a reminder of just how far they have come.

But a 2-1 victory at Real Sociedad in their Europa League opener shows they are not ready to stop there.

It is now 11 years since the Cherries were first promoted to the Premier League, meaning there is now a generation of supporters who will view top-flight football as the norm.

From that perspective then, qualifying and playing in Europe might simply appear the next logical step for a well-run and ambitious club.

"It's a brilliant win in our first European game. It's brilliant for the club and the 2,000 fans from Bournemouth," manager Marco Rose told TNT Sports.

Yet for the vast majority of fans celebrating a famous victory on Thursday, the whole thing still seems surreal.

Just 18 years ago, the club was on the brink. A 10-point deduction for entering administration resulted in their relegation to League Two.

To even stay in the Football League for the 2008-09 season, they had to accept a 17-point deduction and agree not to appeal against the decision after it was ruled that, as they had been unable to agree a Company Voluntary Arrangement, they had not met their terms for exiting administration.

Thoughts of a £100m-rated midfielder picking out a Brazil winger to head Bournemouth to victory in Europe was the stuff of fantasy as the Dorset club battled for survival.

But that now is Bournemouth's reality with Alex Scott swaggering around San Sebastian, showing why there is such a clammer for his signature among top Premier League clubs, and Rayan providing another example of why the Cherries will demand every penny of a reported £130m release clause to let him go.

Bournemouth have nothing to compare it to but this was a proper European away performance.

Up against a Real Sociedad side led by a World Cup-winning forward in Mikel Oyarzabal and who beat Atletico Madrid to win the Copa del Rey last season, they were dominant for 45 minutes.

They suffocated Sociedad with their relentlessness off the ball, winning the ball back high up the pitch time and again and showing the quality on the ball to create chances - even when the defence was set.

But there is an edge to the Basque side and, poor as they had been, that they came out fighting after the break was no surprise.

The adrenaline-fueled exuberance of Rose's side in the first half appeared to catch up with them in the second, but their desire to compete never wavered.

Bournemouth are not known for their defensive resilience and, as Sociedad ramped up the pressure as the game wore on, thoughts might have turned to leads surrendered in each of their first four Premier League games.

But the Cherries, aided by the sharp reflexes of Djordje Petrovic in goal, held on to secure a famous win.

"It was very intense and tough," Rose told TNT Sports.

"Brilliant first half in everything. The way we won balls and the possession high up. In the second half, we needed to suffer because we were not so sharp."

Speaking on BBC Radio Solent, former Cherries full-back Charlie Daniels added: "It is a big occasion. A big moment for the club, and they should be applauded for it."

Bournemouth hold on to win at Sociedad on European bow

Cherries fans hail historic day in San Sebastian

Bournemouth's incredible rise can be traced back to the appointment of Eddie Howe in January 2009.

The former boss guided the Cherries to safety, finishing nine points clear of the relegation zone despite that 17-point deduction.

A mere six and a half years later, Howe - back for his second spell as manager - had taken a transformed Bournemouth to the Premier League.

It was fitting then, that on this latest milestone night for the club, the team was led out by a man involved during Howe's first stint.

Adam Smith joined Bournemouth on loan during the 2010-11 campaign, returned on a permanent deal in 2014 and has been at the club ever since, with approaching 400 league appearances to his name.

"Adam has been with the club for so long," Daniels said. "Dedicated himself to the club, and it's such a proud moment, not only for him, but for his family, his team-mates and old team-mates to see how he's grown - not only as a player but as a man as well.

"To lead out the Cherries on this historical night is fantastic."

Smith also made history of his own, becoming, at 35 years and 141 days, the oldest English outfielder to make their debut in major European competition since Ipswich's Reginald Pickett in 1962.

The club captain will appreciate more than most what a special night this was for Bournemouth.

Things have been far from straightforward for the club, even in recent years, with relegation in 2020 and, since re-establishing themselves in the top-flight, the seemingly annual battle to replace players picked off by Europe's top clubs.

Even qualifying for Europe was not enough to keep hold of manager Andoni Iraola, who returns to the Vitality Stadium with his new club Liverpool on Sunday.

That pattern is unlikely to stop anytime soon but, while there is the prospect of more nights like this one, Bournemouth supporters won't be complaining.

They've seen enough to know that these are the good times.

title: England crush Sri Lanka to seal T20 series win
description: England comfortably chase a below-par target of 146 to thrash Sri Lanka by six wickets and seal the three-match T20 series with a game to spare.
fullText:
Sri Lanka 145-9 (20 overs): Nissanka 37 (21); Dawson 3-32

England 146-4 (12.1 overs): Banton 52* (24); Rathnayake 1-25

England won by six wickets; lead series 2-0

England's impressive T20 form continued as they thrashed Sri Lanka by six wickets in Cardiff to seal the series with a match to spare.

Tom Banton's unbeaten 52 ensured England made light work of chasing a below-par 146, reaching the target in just 12.1 overs.

Jos Buttler and Aneurin Donald raced to an opening stand of 51 in 4.3 overs before they both fell in the space of four balls for 30 and 21 respectively, but England's middle order followed suit in their aggression.

Captain Harry Brook needed to score 49 to break Tilak Varma's record of 336 T20 international runs without being dismissed, and he looked on course, whacking three sixes in his 23 off just eight balls, before he was brilliantly caught by a diving Eshan Malinga.

Banton then took on the charge, clubbing four sixes in his 24-ball knock as England remain unbeaten in the shortest format this summer.

Brendon McCullum's side have now won 22 of their past 25 completed T20s since the start of last summer - a win percentage of 88%, with India (73%) the next best among full-member nations.

England's fluency juxtaposed Sri Lanka's innings as the tourist batters struggled again, limping to 145-9 after being bowled out for just 135 in the opener on Tuesday.

There will be added frustration from this innings, though, as their openers started so brightly by reaching 55-0 from the first five overs.

But Liam Dawson took two wickets in the final over of the powerplay to halt their momentum and the middle order failed to recover, losing 9-90 thereafter and adding just 12 from a dire final four overs.

Dawson finished with 3-32 and Jamie Overton 2-23, while Sonny Baker impressed again with his pace and control in a miserly spell of 1-15, including a wicket maiden in the 19th over.

The series concludes at Old Trafford on Saturday and is followed by three one-day internationals.

Though it is proving to be a mismatched series so far, England are building a well-balanced line-up under Brook's leadership and have barely broken sweat in notching a 2-0 lead.

Sri Lanka's explosive start, led by Pathum Nissanka, who top-scored with 37, was the only time England have been on the back foot, but it was the ever-reliable Dawson who dragged it back, having become a mainstay in Brook's T20 line-up.

The two soft dismissals highlighted Sri Lanka's woes - Lahiru Udara was caught at mid-on and Kamil Mishara chipped one straight back to the slow left-arm spinner.

What followed was a series of soft dismissals, most caught trying to find the boundary, as Overton and Baker hammered away at a good length before Archer, who had started expensively, claimed two wickets at the death to revive his own figures.

Sri Lanka managed just two sixes in their innings compared to England's 10, with it being only the seventh time their top five have all hit at least one in T20 internationals.

Newcomer Donald started the carnage, ramping Dushmantha Chameera's first ball over the ropes, before Buttler joined the party and Brook then launched three of his own into the stands.

England's intent was clear from the fact Donald's strike-rate of 161.54 was the lowest of the top five. Spinner Wanindu Hasaranga took most of the damage as he conceded 42 off just three overs, with a couple disappearing out of the ground.

Banton, one of few batters to miss out in England's 254-4 on Tuesday, made the most of his opportunity to produce a fine finish by sweeping and striking firmly down the ground.

England have set themselves up nicely to finish unbeaten in T20s this summer after thrashing India 4-0 earlier in the year.

title: Champion Van Gerwen loses in first round to Gurney
description: Defending champion Michael van Gerwen falls to a 6-5 defeat by Daryl Gurney in the opening round of the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.
fullText:
Defending champion Michael van Gerwen fell to a 6-5 defeat by Daryl Gurney in the opening round of the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.

Northern Ireland's Gurney raced into a 3-0 lead before the Dutch top seed reeled off five consecutive legs to put himself on the brink of victory.

However, Gurney, who was drafted in as a late replacement when Lourence Ilagan withdrew from the 32-man field, responded by taking the ninth leg.

And when Van Gerwen missed six match darts, he was able to level the match at 5-5 and win the decider with the throw.

Gurney will now take on England's Ross Smith in the last 16 on Saturday after he advanced past Kevin Doets 6-3.

World number one Luke Littler will get under way on Friday against former UK Open champion Danny Noppert, having recently whitewashed the Dutchman 6-0 on his way to winning the Czech Darts Open.

World number two Luke Humphries also emerged victorious in another England versus Netherlands encounter, progressing 6-4 against Jermaine Wattimena.

Dutch number one Gian van Veen gained a measure of revenge for the home fans with a 6-2 triumph over Chris Dobey.

Dirk van Duijvenbode fought back from 4-1 down to defeat Sweden's Viktor Tingstrom 6-4, while Ryan Searle threw four 180s as he dispatched former world champion Rob Cross 6-2.

Searle goes on to play Josh Rock, who won the last three legs to edge out Stephen Bunting 6-5.

Karel Sedlacek marked his debut at the tournament with a 6-4 win over New Zealander Ben Robb and will take on Van Veen next.

title: 'Just the beginning' - Samba, 17, steals Man City show
description: Floyd Samba's scintillating debut stole the show at Etihad Stadium but also took the headlines away from another high-profile teenager in Manchester.
fullText:
Floyd Samba's scintillating first-team debut not only stole the show at Etihad Stadium on Thursday but also snatched all the headlines away from another high-profile teenager in Manchester.

Website articles, social media posts and column inches have been filled this week with the news that highly rated 15-year-old forward JJ Gabriel is on the verge of leaving Manchester United.

But that particular saga will be overshadowed in Friday's football cuttings by 17-year-old Samba's stunning bow on the professional stage, scoring twice in Manchester City's 5-0 Carabao Cup third-round thrashing of Norwich City.

Samba was prolific in City's under-18 side last season and those impressive performances led to him being promoted to the first-team set-up by new manager Enzo Maresca this summer.

The show of faith is already being repaid.

"I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team," Samba told BBC Radio 5 Live. "To get a debut like that is mind-blowing.

"I couldn't believe it myself - but that is just the beginning, I have got a big career ahead of me. It was a great debut.

"I spoke to all of them [first-team players], they have all been brilliant with me - before the game, giving me advice like 'play your game, be you' - those words have given me confidence and helped me score those two goals today."

Samba with debut double as Man City thrash Norwich

The youngster joined City's academy at under-nine level and he really started to make a name for himself last term.

Samba scored 24 goals and provided 10 assists in an eye-catching first full season with the under-18s, including curling home a stunning free-kick to help City win the FA Youth Cup final against rivals Manchester United in May.

On his debut, Samba played the entire 90 minutes and fully grasped his opportunity.

With City struggling for openings, Samba broke the deadlock by flicking home a header - he celebrated by blowing a kiss in the direction of family and friends in the stands, before curling in a delightful second later in the game.

Samba was afforded a generous ovation towards the end of the game when being deservedly named man of the match.

"[I'm] satisfied not just for the goals but for the performance too," said manager Maresca.

"I asked him in the last three, four days - when I decided to play him as nine - he said he never played there. He is not a nine for sure, but he was good.

"He is young, full of energy, strong, can finish, can set [players up]. He made some good decisions in the first half. I am happy but they are young and we have to go slowly, slowly.

"Hopefully we can give him more chances."

The Samba surname will be familiar to those of a certain age who have followed the Premier League.

Floyd is the son of former Blackburn and QPR defender Christopher, who played 171 top-flight matches for those two sides, as well as a further 12 in the Championship with Aston Villa.

The City forward is the younger of two brothers at the club, with Tyrone also involved in the youth team, and will now be aiming to play more first-team minutes after an exciting debut.

As a fleet-footed forward, Floyd could not be more of a different player to his dad Christopher, who was a no-nonsense towering centre-back.

"Coming from under-21s to first-team training, that is a big jump," added Samba. "The sessions are more tiring, you have to run more - they demand more of you and you have to cope with it."

Former Norwich striker Chris Sutton added on BBC Radio 5 Live: "Absolutely brilliant moment for Floyd. His dad was in the stadium and will be extremely proud. It's the journey, he has been nurtured at Man City, got his moment and what a night for him.

"He has given Enzo Maresca a bit of food for thought moving forward. Of course, he is not going to play ahead of Erling Haaland but it is a great evening for him and good for his development.

"Maresca can think he can trust him a little bit more."
